page: Amazon Web Services g7e.48xlarge is a high-density, accelerator-driven server instance powered by the AWS Nitro Hypervisor. It features 192 vCPUs derived from 96 physical cores on dual-threaded Intel Xeon 8559C processors running at a base frequency of 2.4 GHz, backed by a 320 MB L3 cache and support for Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instruction sets. System memory comprises 2048 GB of DDR5 RAM running at 6 GHz, providing 10.67 GB per physical core. For acceleration and high-speed local throughput, the instance incorporates eight NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 GPUs providing a combined 768 GB of VRAM, 15.2 TB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a baseline network bandwidth of 400 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the g7e.48xlarge delivers top-tier multi-threaded compute and memory performance. Multi-core stress-ng tests achieved a score of 169929.73, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression reached 1101.51 GB/sec. Memory read bandwidth measured 447.23 GB/sec uncached, while write performance reached 190.94 GB/sec. Specialized workloads demonstrated high throughput, including 201.69 million Redis SET operations per second, 207.79 GB/sec in static web serving, and strong LLM inference processing rates across 135M, 7B, and 70B parameter models, reaching 1269.37 tokens per second for 70B model prompt processing.

Given its hardware density, the instance offers high consolidation efficiency for demanding enterprise workloads, trading off low baseline hardware footprints for high throughput per node. The combination of 8 GPUs with 768 GB VRAM, extensive system RAM, high NVMe storage capacity, and 400 Gbps network capacity makes the g7e.48xlarge best suited for graphics-intensive rendering, large language model inference and training, high-throughput database processing, and data science workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services g7e.48xlarge is an accelerator-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, designed for compute-intensive and graphics-heavy enterprise workloads. It incorporates 192 vCPUs across 96 physical Intel Xeon 8559C cores operating at 2.4 GHz with 320 MB L3 cache and AMX acceleration, paired with 2048 GB of DDR5 memory. The server is equipped with eight NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 GPUs supplying 768 GB of VRAM, along with 15.2 TB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline 400 Gbps network bandwidth. Benchmark results confirm top-tier multi-core execution, fast uncached memory read bandwidth of 447.23 GB/sec, and exceptional throughput in Redis operations and LLM inference. This system trades small-scale modularity for massive per-node processing density, making it well suited for large language model deployment, real-time ray tracing, distributed data science, and high-performance database execution.
